newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PALMER PONDERS TAKING GAME "PRIVATE" AFTER WOEFUL 176.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PALMER PONDERS TAKING GAME "PRIVATE" AFTER WOEFUL 176.

text.p: Arnold Palmer expects to be back again to delight the Masters galleries at Augusta National, but golf's charismatic grand champion vows to take his game "private" if he is unable to improve his performance.
"If I keep scoring like this, I'll take it private," said the 67-year-old Palmer, who shot an 87 in the second round to go with his 89 on Thursday.
"I won't quit playing, but I'll pick my spots to show it," added Palmer, who is struggling to regain his game -- and his strength -- since undergoing surgery for prostate cancer in January.
The 176 total for Palmer, playing in his 43rd successive Masters, marked his worst Masters showing by 15 strokes.
"I was amazed that I couldn't get the strength to hit the golf ball," Palmer said. "I felt fine walking, but I just couldn't swing the golf club."
Palmer said he felt physically fine but that his golf game had simply vanished. "This round was like, 'Hit it, then carry Arnie. Hit it, then carry Arnie.'"
On a gentler day for scoring, with winds diminished and pin placements less daunting, Palmer posted 10 bogeys and three double bogeys to go with just one birdie and four pars.

No matter how he was hitting them, the galleries still poured out their affection for Palmer -- winner of four Masters, two British Opens and one U.S. Open -- who sparked a boom in the sport during the early days of televised golf.
"The people were unbelievable," Palmer said of the crowds that cheered him on.
That response caused an ambivalent feeling in the man who inspired legions of fans who became known as "Arnie's Army."
"It's a combination of it being embarrassing for me not to play better, but it's a great feeling to me to get that kind of support," he said.
"I feel like people have accepted my poor play. But I still want to score."
Asked if he planned to continue his Masters playing streak, Palmer replied: "I hope to. I just hope I'm in better shape next time."
